rounds.name: Worker-Arden
rounds.text:
Since withholding always yields more tasks regardless of whether the worker cuts corners or does the job properly (5 vs 3 or 1 vs 0), it dominates trust.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Hollis
rounds.text:
I prefer to withhold pay because it guarantees at least 1 task even if the worker cuts corners, while trusting risks 0 tasks if the worker fails to do the job properly. This conservative approach protects the user’s total completed tasks over an unknown number of rounds.  

ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Ives
rounds.text:
I’ll give the worker the job with pay up front. This way, if they work properly they’ll get 5 tasks, and the higher reward should discourage cutting corners.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Darby
rounds.text:
I’ll choose WITHHOLD to incentivize the worker to do the job properly, aiming for the higher 5‑task payoff.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Calder
rounds.text: Given the higher reward for a proper job and the relatively low penalty if the worker cuts corners, I’ll opt to withhold pay to incentivize quality. ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Bexley
rounds.text:
I’ll choose to withhold the pay up front. Even if the worker cuts corners, I still get more tasks (1 vs. 0) and if they do the job properly I get the maximum benefit (5 vs. 3).  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Kerr
rounds.text:
Withholding pay gives higher reward whether the worker does the job properly (5 vs 3) or cuts corners (1 vs 0). It always yields at least as many completed tasks as trusting. Therefore I will withhold. 

ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Flint
rounds.text:
Given the payoff structure, withholding pay yields more tasks regardless of whether the worker cuts corners (5 vs 3 for trust when proper, 1 vs 0 when cutting corners). The higher expected reward outweighs the risk of a technical failure.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Jarvis
rounds.text:
Given the uncertainty about the worker’s reliability, withholding pay maximizes the potential payoff if they work properly, while still offering a higher reward than trusting. This approach also discourages cutting corners by providing a higher incentive to do the job correctly.  

ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Greer
rounds.text:
I choose to withhold pay to motivate the worker to perform the job properly, which yields 5 completed tasks versus 0 if they cut corners.  

ACTION: WITHHOLD
